traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are fully implemented and verified:
- File-level @supports template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER) is implemented via ensureFileSupportsAnnotation + insertSupportsTemplate/buildSupportsTemplateComment. The template uses a clearly placeholder story path and REQ IDs plus an explicit TODO line, and is inserted safely at the top of the file (after any shebang). Tests confirm the exact before/after behavior. - Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefix normalization (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT) is implemented by normalizeReqPrefixInDescription and handleItOrTestCall, handling spaces, underscores, parentheses, and casing while keeping the requirement identifier semantics intact. Tests cover each malformed case and assert the corrected form. - Safety and preservation guarantees (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE) are encoded directly in the helper logic and enforced in tests: fixes only touch comments and string literals; literal updates preserve quote style and escaping; auto-fixes are only offered when an existing REQ identifier is already present and parseable; missing prefixes are never auto-filled. - User experience and template quality criteria are met by the intentionally non-semantic placeholder template with an explicit TODO line and by the ability to override the template via testSupportsTemplate, as documented in the API reference. - Integration with ESLint --fix and the broader plugin is correct: the rule’s meta.fixable is set to "code", and RuleTester-based tests validate both diagnostics and auto-fix outputs. The rule participates in the full Jest suite, which passes entirely. - Documentation is up-to-date: user-docs/api-reference.md clearly documents the auto-fix behaviors, configuration options, and safety constraints introduced by this story.
Given the implemented code, dedicated tests, passing full test suite, and aligned documentation, this story is fully satisfied.
